newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ELANDSRAND DEAL OPENS ORE WEALTH FOR ANGLO.
newsitem.headline: ELANDSRAND DEAL OPENS ORE WEALTH FOR ANGLO.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa said its flagship mine Elandsrand's acquisition of Deelkraal, in a 420 million rand deal, allows it to exploit the shared ore body to its maximum potential.

Announcing the deal on Tuesday, chairman of Anglogold Bobby Godsell said the Deelkraal-Elandsrand merger was significant for South Africa's mining industry in that it lifted the veil on a new age of shared mineral rights and freed boundaries.

"I think its important for the South African mining industry if we could take down the farm fences, swap mineral rights etc. We're informed of how we can extract satisfactorily the optimum amount of gold from the ground where it lies in South Africa."
"Elandsrand is the flagship of Anglo gold companies. It's firing on all pistons and doing very well. This (deal) gives us the best chance of extracting all the possible ore," he said.
The transaction sees mining house Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd relinquish 100 percent of the share capital of Deelkraal Gold Mining Co Ltd to Elandsrand Gold Mining Co.
Deelkraal shareholders will be issued with 20 new Elandsrand ordinary shares for every 100 Deelkraal ordinary shares held, and Deelkraal will subsequently be delisted.
"Looking at the current share value of Elandsrand we're talking about 420 million rand as the value of the deal," said Gold Fields executive director John Hopwood.
Godsell said Anglo fully acknowledged and was comfortable with the fact that it was acquiring Deelkraal at a premium.
"We're happy with the dilution of Elandsrand and the value we're paying in scrip terms," he said.
Deelkraal closed Tuesday on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange 35 cents higher at 380 cents per share, while Elandsrand finished 100 cents firmer at 21 rand per share.
Godsell said that Anglo used "conservative" gold price estimates in calculating the viability of the deal and believed "the project would be able to sustain a couple of years of weak prices".
The takeover is conditional on satisfactory completion of a due diligence investigation by Elandsrand which was expected to be completed on or about April 18.
Anglo said it had announced the deal, prior to the due diligence being completed, based on certain assumptions about the viability of the project.
It added that if any of those ssumptions were not verified the companies would go back to the drawing board.
Elandsrand produced 4,242 kg of gold in teh December quarter, while Deelkraal produced 1,823.4 kg of gold.
The deal means that Elandsrand inherits Deelkraal's cash overdraft and unspent capital expenditure.
Anglo said that the merger gives Elandsrand the flexibility to expand production if it so wished, but added that any such a decision would hinge on an improvment in the gold price.
Gold Fields' Hopwood said that Mercury Asset Management held about nine percent of Deelkraal and that the group had not yet spoken to them about the merger.
